findings.title: Do not let retry bookkeeping abort the entire reminder batch
findings.body: The catch block now awaits a Prisma update without handling failures from that update. If a reminder is deleted while this batch is running (for example, during booking cancellation or workflow removal), the update throws because the row no longer exists; a database outage likewise causes this error handler to throw. Previously the per-reminder catch logged the error and continued. Now the request exits early and all remaining reminders in the batch are skipped. Handle retry-update failures separately so one failed or removed reminder does not prevent unrelated SMS reminders from being scheduled.

findings.title: Increment retry counts atomically instead of writing a stale snapshot
findings.body: Both failure paths assign retryCount using the value read by findMany at the start of the request. If cron requests overlap and both attempt the same unscheduled reminder, they can read the same count and then write the same incremented value, losing one failed attempt. This allows more scheduling failures than the intended two-attempt limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than computing the new count from the fetched reminder.
